items.title: George P. Fleming Interview, 1984-10-06
items.q: Louie Nelson's giving you lessons that's pretty good ... he also gave me a lot of pointers about life

ctx.x: well he did a lot of Tommy Doss's arrangements a lot of Tommy Doss's he did that and with ease he used to sit on and just broom right out in the head like a megaphone during that time the trombone player used to blow in a big megaphone quiet the tone down it wouldn't be so brassy he would get there during that time trumpet players had derbies on the stand and you had mutes that you used during that time for different effects I don't see them maybe in the big bands now they might still use these type of mutes
what you mentioned Louie Nelson's technique of breathing what was that what did he tell you about breathing

well he told me that his teacher the one I don't remember his name he took the lesson from told him the important thing of playing that horn is to learn how to breathe and that is from the diaphragm and by the high notes he used to hit it was from the diaphragm and not from the lip and it took a long time for me to understand because mine was more lip power than it was any other method that's the only weapon I knew
